To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the online non-cliarvoyant scheduling algorithms LS, LL-GREED, and LL-SIMPLE have asymptotic average-case performances of M/(M-C+1), M/(M-3C+1), and M/(M-(C+1)2), respectively.

the online non-clairovyant scheduling algorithm LL-GREED has the best performance among the three algorithms for the class of wide task graph, and that algorithm LS produces even better schedule than LL-GREED due to break of the boundary between levels.

(i) the average-case performance bound for LL-SIMPLE is M/(M-(C+1) C-1) when task sizes are distributed uniformly in the range [C..C]; (ii) the average-case performances of LL-GREEDy and LS are very close and both are significantly better than LL-SIMPLY; and (iii) the average-case bound for LS is M/(M-C C-1) in the limit as C goes to infinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the average-case performance analysis of online non-clairyovant scheduling algorithms.
the average-case performance analysis of online non-cliarvoyant scheduling algorithms for parallel task systems, where tasks are released one-by-one, each with a fixed number of processors.
average-case analysis and experimental study of the performance of online nonclairvoyant scheduling for parallel tasks with precedence constraint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LL-SIMPLE, LL-GREEDy and LS are the best online algorithms in the literature for scheduling parallel tasks with precedence and communication constraints.
the best algorithm for online non-clairoyant scheduling of parallel task graphs with precedence constraints is LL-SIMPLE, followed by LL-GREED.
LL-SIMPLE is the best choice for online scheduling of parallel tasks, while LL-GREEDy and LS can be used when more accurate performance is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the average-case performance bound M/(M-(C+1)2) for LL-SIMPLE is a good approximation for the performance of the online non-clairoyant algorithms for scheduling tasks on M processors.
the average-case performance bound for LL-SIMPLE is accurate for most task graphs.
the performance bound of LL-SIMPLE is asymptotically tight and LL-SIMPLE performs well in practice.

online non-clairvoynat scheduling algorithms can be designed with a good average-case performance bound and that the performance of online algorithms can be improved by using a more sophisticated scheduling algorithm for scheduling independent tasks in the level.
the online scheduling algorithms for parallel tasks can have good performance on wide task graphs.
